newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait Stock Exchange sets trading value high.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait Stock Exchange sets trading value high.

text.p: Trading value on the Kuwait Stock Exchange (KSE) soared on Monday to a record 125.8 million dinars ($414 million) during the 2-1/2-hour session.
"The market is on fire," said an official of the record- breaking trading week.

The index, which rose 40.9 points on Saturday setting a new high of 2,338.2 points, closed up six points on Monday at 2,334 -- a 22.5 percent rise since the start of the year. The index rose by an average 40 percent a year for the previous two years.

Total trading value for 1996 was almost $20 billion with a daily average of under $100 million compared with Monday's $414 million while the daily average for the previous two days was around $280 million.

KSE Director-General Hisham al-Oteibi told Reuters on Monday that trading value on the Kuwait exchange represented about 80 percent of total trading value on eight official bourses in fellow Arab states.
He attributed the larger trading value to "confidence in the market and the economic policies of the state and more firms entering the market (new listings)."

Although trading on the Kuwait market is open only to Gulf Arab nationals from Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Oman, Bahrain and Qatar, trade value last year was about four times larger than total trading value on the seven other official Arab exchanges.
